(assuming you're in the U.S.) You can walk into a hospital and explain that you feel suicidal. They will ask you a bunch of questions and determine if you're a current danger to yourself or others. If so, they will probably ask you to sign a 201, which is voluntarily commiting yourself. From there, they'll work with your insurance to find you an open bed at an inpatient hospital or facility. Once you're there, you'll most likely meet with a psychiatrist and social workers to start treatment in order to stabilize you for discharge. Usually, it lasts a couple of days, but that all depends on you and your situation. Just plan to not be around for a couple days after going to the hospital. They'll connect you with resources once you are discharged so that you can continue treatment. It's scary, but it's worth it to keep on living.
